answer: Each account can request work, but only completed jobs with a bonded stake earn reputation: a requester escrows payment, a worker stakes funds, and an independent reviewer releases the escrow or slashes the worker’s bond for fraud. Splitting into sybils does not multiply influence, because each new identity must lock fresh capital and earn a track record through costly jobs. A spiral of disposable accounts therefore burns fees and risks forfeited stakes; even a sable haven for cheap identities cannot make trust free.
